columns.rationale: Order identifier with null_rate 0.0 and 4000 distinct values over 5000 rows (samples like ORD-100001); renamed from 'Order ID' to snake_case order_id.
Landed INTEGER with null_rate 0.0 and 7 distinct values (min 1, max 7), consistent with a line number within an order; renamed from CamelCase LineNo.

320 distinct values with null_rate 0.0; samples mix product codes (85123A, 10002) with non-product markers (BANK CHARGES, DOT), so the column is kept as text and a derived flag marks the non-product records.
Derived boolean set true when sku is a non-product marker such as the sampled BANK CHARGES and DOT values, letting consumers filter adjustment-style records without losing them.

Samples disagree on representation ('-3', '2.0', 'three'), so a numeric cast is not safe from evidence and the column is kept as VARCHAR; null_rate 0.002 (10 nulls) so it is nullable with nulls retained.

Landed DECIMAL(38,9) with null_rate 0.0; all samples have at most two decimal places (0.42, 4.95, 7.5) within min -5.0 and max 1250.0, supporting a cast to DECIMAL(10,2); negative values are retained as landed.
All 10 samples are ISO-shaped timestamps (e.g. '2024-01-05 09:15:00') with null_rate 0.0 and 1880 distinct values, supporting a VARCHAR to TIMESTAMP cast.

Samples show mutually inconsistent formats ('01/07/2024', '07.01.2024', '2024-1-9', 'Jan 9 2024') plus non-date values ('TBD', empty string), so no date cast is safe; null_rate 0.264 so nulls are retained.
Sparsely populated with null_rate 0.97 (4850 nulls) and 140 distinct values; retained nullable as-is since the populated samples are well-formed addresses.

Free-text field with null_rate 0.61 and 2100 distinct values; some samples are truncated at the 120-character cap and all values, including instruction-like strings, are untrusted source data retained verbatim.

null_rate 0.0 with 5 distinct values that are case variants of three states (CANCELLED/cancelled, Shipped/shipped, pending); kept as landed text so the casing inconsistency stays visible for a reviewed normalization decision.
All 4 distinct values (Y, N, yes, no) map unambiguously to booleans, supporting a VARCHAR to BOOLEAN cast; null_rate 0.012 (60 nulls) so nulls are retained.
Single distinct value 'legacy_pos' with null_rate 0.0; retained for lineage since future loads may add other systems.
Profiled with is_airbyte_metadata true; capture-tool identifier, not a business column, dropped per policy.
Profiled with is_airbyte_metadata true; extraction timestamp with only 2 distinct values from one sync window, dropped as a capture artifact.
Profiled with is_airbyte_metadata true; single distinct value '{}' carrying no business content, dropped as a capture artifact.

decisions.rationale: The profile reports row_count 5000 with duplicate_row_rate 0.08, so roughly 400 rows are exact copies; silver removes rows identical across all retained business columns, keeping one copy each.

Order ID has 4000 distinct values over 5000 rows and LineNo ranges 1 to 7 with no nulls in either, so one row per (order_id, line_no) is the smallest defensible grain after exact-duplicate removal; a human should measure uniqueness before approval.
qty samples mix integers, decimal text ('2.0'), negatives ('-3'), and words ('three'); no cast is safe, so the column stays VARCHAR for downstream parsing under review.
ship_date mixes at least five date formats plus 'TBD' and empty strings with null_rate 0.264; no deterministic date cast covers all samples, so the raw text is retained.
customer_email is null in 97% of rows (4850 nulls); the column is retained nullable with no imputation and no row drops.
notes is 61% null free text; some values are truncated at the 120-character cap and some read like instructions, but all are treated strictly as source data and carried through unchanged.
status has 5 distinct values that are case variants of 3 states; normalization is deferred to review rather than silently collapsed, so consumers must compare case-insensitively for now.
All 4 distinct is_gift values (Y, N, yes, no) map cleanly to true/false; 60 nulls (rate 0.012) are retained as null.
unit_price samples carry at most two decimal places within min -5.0 and max 1250.0, so DECIMAL(38,9) is tightened to DECIMAL(10,2); negative prices are retained as landed and flagged in limitations.
sku samples include non-product markers BANK CHARGES and DOT; is_non_product_record is derived so consumers can filter adjustment-style records without data loss.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are flagged is_airbyte_metadata in the profile and carry no business content, so all three are dropped.

purpose: silver_orders is the cleaned order-line table derived from bronze.messy_orders (5000 landed rows from the legacy_pos system). It standardizes column names to snake_case, removes exact duplicate rows, casts order timestamps, unit prices, and the gift flag to typed columns, drops Airbyte capture metadata, and declares a grain of one row per order_id and line_no. It feeds order-level analytics and any downstream gold aggregation of order lines.
usage: Read one row per (order_id, line_no) after exact-duplicate removal. Filter is_non_product_record = false to analyze product lines only, since skus like BANK CHARGES and DOT mark adjustment records. qty and ship_date remain raw text and must be parsed deliberately; status carries mixed casing, so compare case-insensitively (e.g. lower(status)) until a normalization is approved. Nulls in qty, ship_date, customer_email, notes, and is_gift are retained, not imputed.
limitations: Cleanup could not resolve qty (mixed numeric and word samples such as 'three') or ship_date (at least five formats plus 'TBD', null_rate 0.264), both retained as VARCHAR. customer_email is 97% null and notes 61% null; notes values are truncated at 120 characters in the profile and contain untrusted free text retained verbatim. status casing is inconsistent across its 5 distinct values, unit_price includes negative values down to -5.0 as landed, and the declared (order_id, line_no) grain has not yet been measured against the warehouse.
